hero_product.title: Talk to the {word}
hero_product.lead: Free, open source voice ATC for Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024. Speak in your own words — a controller answers in real phraseology, from clearance to gate. Everything runs on your PC.
hero_product.ptt: Hold your push-to-talk key and speak normally — no scripts, no menus.
hero_wordmark.title: A voice controller for MSFS 2024 that understands you. Free, open source, offline.
hero_strip.title: Every flight gets a strip. Every strip gets a voice.
hero_strip.lead: WilcoATC reads your flight plan, prints your strip and runs the frequency — clearance to gate, in real phraseology.
how.title: Three steps, then you are on frequency.
how.1.d: Any headset works. Say something, watch the bars move, done.
how.2.d: A keyboard key, a joystick button, or voice-activated. The panel’s own button works either way.
how.3.d: From SimBrief or by hand. Aircraft, position and weather come straight from the simulator.
features.title: A controller, not a recording.
features.airspace.d: Every station in range, the traffic around you, coverage and your filed route on a real map — following the aircraft.
features.1.d: Ask in plain language. The readback comes back the way it is actually said on frequency.
features.2.d: A beat before keying up, never quite the same loudness twice, the occasional “uh”. Rare on purpose.
features.3.d: METARs from the NOAA Aviation Weather Center — or the simulator wins, if you prefer your own.
features.4.d: Touchdown rate, how smooth it was, and the flight against its SimBrief schedule.
modules.title: The whole flight, not just the radio.
module.atc.d: Delivery to the gate, every position on its real frequency, with correct phraseology.
module.cabin.d: Boarding, the safety demonstration and the captain's welcome, never over the radio.
module.copilot.d: Callouts at your speeds, what they notice unasked, and radio calls you hand over.
module.checklists.d: Challenge and response, each answer checked against the simulator.
module.traffic.d: Airliners on the field's real stands and taxiways, in their own liveries.
module.ground.d: Stairs, belt loaders, fuel and the tug at each aircraft's own doors.

faq.title: Questions pilots ask.
faq.1.q: Does it work with my simulator?
faq.1.a: WilcoATC is built for Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 only. MSFS 2020 and X-Plane are not supported.
faq.2.q: Do I need to know the phraseology?
faq.2.a: No. Say it the way you would explain it to a friend; the controller understands pilots and replies in standard phraseology, so you learn it as you go.
faq.3.a: Every airport in your simulator with a published frequency — over 18 000. Smaller fields use UNICOM / traffic advisory procedures.
faq.4.q: Does it talk to other add-ons?
faq.4.a: It reads your SimBrief plan and the simulator’s live weather, and it follows the aircraft wherever you are. Nothing to configure.
faq.5.a: Yes. WilcoATC is open source under the {license} licence, and speech recognition, voices and the controller all run locally — no paid tier, no trial. If it helps you, star the repo or send a pull request.
